title: Secretary of State of Iowa

context.text: Neither primary was contested on June 2, 2026: Paul Pate (R) received 183,874 votes and Ryan Peterman (D) 176,708.
The Iowa Secretary of State's general-election candidate list (updated Aug. 19, 2026) shows only Pate (Republican) and Peterman (Democratic) for Secretary of State.

candidates.name: Paul Pate
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the June 2 Republican primary.

priorities.text: Voter participation and election integrity together, with a 'layered approach': voter ID, paper ballots, post-election audits, pre-election equipment testing, absentee ballot tracking and bipartisan poll workers.
Modernize business filings: he cites Fast Track Filing, a redesigned website and a 24/7 call center.

record.text: The office was recognized by the U.S. Election Assistance Commission with a Clearie Award and by the National Association of Secretaries of State as an IDEAs finalist (announced August 3, 2026).
Selected as co-chair of the National Association of Secretaries of State Business Services Committee for 2026-27.
Issued a September 2026 notice that Iowans may begin voting absentee October 14 for the November 3 general election, by mail or in person.

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site appears not to have been updated since 2022. Record items are routine office announcements; rules and certifications were not itemized.

candidates.name: Ryan Peterman
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced unopposed from the June 2 Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Make sure 'every eligible Iowan can vote, that elections are fair and secure, and that politics never gets in the way of doing the job right.'
Partner with county auditors; he says he has met with them in small towns and big cities across the state.

candidates.researchNotes: No Ballotpedia survey or detailed policy pages were found; the campaign site's 'Why I'm Running' page is the main source.
